blind_spots.blind_spot: Optics-first shop feeding a TAK ecosystem it never talks about on its own site
blind_spots.operator_reality: Their Tactical AR system lives or dies on the ATAK data pipeline over tactical radios — DDIL bandwidth, mesh drops, and CoT message discipline — yet all ~645 public words are about displays, holography, and packaging, none about the comms path that actually delivers the situational awareness.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Founders and staff are electro-optics and lithography specialists (MIT Media Lab holography lineage); the network side is someone else's GFE in their mental model.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: an integrated workflow that spans optics, mechanics, electronics, software and firmware development – all accomplished in-house

blind_spots.blind_spot: Skunkworks prototype culture with no visible path through accreditation to a program
blind_spots.operator_reality: A helmet display carrying classified SA data onto a soldier needs the hosting software to survive RMF/ATO and the program office to fund it past prototype; 'quick turn' one-offs stall exactly at the valley Barry works — nothing in their language mentions ATO, RMF, STIG, or an acquisition pathway.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Thirty-five years of surviving on quick-turn custom R&D jobs rewards fast prototypes, not the slow advocacy chain that turns one into a fielded program.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Skunkworks quick turn engineering and problem solving

blind_spots.blind_spot: No sustainment or training story for hardware worn by an E-5
blind_spots.operator_reality: Helmet- and weapon-mounted displays in the field mean battery logistics, spares, and a 20-minute-trained sergeant doing maintenance; a 19-person Vermont shop doing 'limited run production' has no field-service or training footprint in any of its language.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: As a component/prototype supplier they have always handed hardware to a customer engineer, never owned unit-level fielding.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Quick turn prototypes and limited run production
